newsitem.title: KENYA: Nervous foreigners pull out of Kenya bill auction.
newsitem.headline: Nervous foreigners pull out of Kenya bill auction.

text.p: Foreign investors pulled out of the Kenyan treasury bill market on Thursday citing uncertainty despite the central bank's efforts to woo investors by raising interest rates on bills, bank officials said.
The bank said it received applications worth 7.430 billion shillings ($106 million), half of the total 14 billion shillings offered for auction.

"The shortfall is attributed to foreign investors who have decided to liquidate their investments citing uncertainty arising from the recent lapse of the financial arrangement with the International Monetary Fund .. as the main reason for their pulling out," a Central Bank of Kenya statement said.
The bank was referring to a decision by the IMF to cancel a $205 million package citing its concern over corruption that shook currency and equity markets in the worst turbulence since October 1993.
The total value of the auction was $200 million.

The bank appealed to investors to continue investing in government bills since the finance minister recently indicated that the government would be prepared to pay higher rates to finance government borrowing.

The interest rate on the benchmark 90-day t-bill edged to 18.783 percent compared to 18.199 percent last week. The bank sold a total of 7.21 billion shillings of the bill compared to 4.968 billion shillings last week.
The bank sold 74 million shillings of the 182-day t-bill at an average yield of 19.249 percent from 44 million shillings at 19.062 billion shillings.
